chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:

When you have prayed Zuhr, the time of Asr has entered, except that there is an optional prayer (subha) before it — that is up to you. If you wish, you may prolong it, and if you wish, you may shorten it.

key_terms.الظُّهْر: Zuhr — the obligatory noon prayer, one of the five daily prayers in Islam
key_terms.الْعَصْر: Asr — the obligatory afternoon prayer, performed in the latter part of the day
key_terms.سُبْحَة: Subha/Nafila — the optional supererogatory prayer offered between Zuhr and Asr; not obligatory but recommended

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Asr prayer begin according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a key ruling in Islamic prayer law: the time for Asr prayer begins immediately upon completion of Zuhr prayer, without any mandatory waiting period. However, there is traditionally a brief window designated for the optional supererogatory prayer (known as the subha or nafila of Zuhr) to be performed between Zuhr and Asr. The Imam confirms this optional prayer is voluntary and discretionary — the worshipper may extend or shorten it as they wish.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik,

‘Heasws said: ‘When you have prayed Salāt Al-Zohr, so the time for Al-Asr has entered until there happens to be an Optional (Salāt) in front of it. So that is up to you. If you so desire to, you prolong, and if you so desire to, you shorten (the Optional Salāt)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Misma’ ibn ‘Abd Malik who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When you complete al-Dhuhr Salah (prayer), it is time for al- ‘Asr Salah (prayer) except that before it there is Nafl (optional Salah (prayer) and it is up to you to make it lengthy or a short one.’”
